topic: How a 600 dollar car repair becomes 8400 dollars of debt
title: How $600 Became $8,400

visual_bible.her: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket over a grey sweater, jeans and white sneakers
visual_bible.her kitchen: a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, a wooden table under the window, two mismatched chairs, and a corkboard covered in pinned paper
visual_bible.her car: a small faded red hatchback with a dented rear bumper

scenes.narration: On a Tuesday morning her car makes a sound it has never made before. Then it stops making any sound at all.
scenes.image_prompt: a small faded red hatchback with a dented rear bumper stopped on the shoulder of a highway, hazard lights on, early morning, grey sky, empty road ahead

scenes.narration: She is nine minutes from work and forty miles from home. She does not know it yet, but this is the most expensive morning of her life.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket over a grey sweater, sitting in the driver's seat of a stopped car on a highway shoulder, both hands still on the wheel, face blank and unsmiling, grey sky and empty road through the windshield

scenes.narration: The engine is silent and warm. She looks at it the way anyone looks at an engine, which is to say hopefully, and without any idea.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket over a grey sweater, jeans and white sneakers, standing at the open hood of a small faded red hatchback on a highway shoulder under a grey sky, shoulders dropped, mouth tight, staring down into the engine

scenes.narration: The shop can take it today. That is the good news. She writes their number on the back of her hand because her phone is at four percent.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket over a grey sweater, standing alone on a highway shoulder under a heavy grey sky, holding one hand up close to her face and reading a phone number written in blue pen across the back of it, jaw set, no phone anywhere

scenes.narration: Month one. The bill is six hundred dollars.
scenes.image_prompt: the words MONTH ONE in large plain black capitals, centred, nothing else

scenes.narration: The gearbox has gone. Six hundred dollars, and everyone agrees it could have been worse, and everyone is right about that.
scenes.image_prompt: a small faded red hatchback with a dented rear bumper raised on a repair shop lift, tools and parts around it, strip lights overhead

scenes.narration: She has four hundred dollars. She also has a credit card she has never really used, sitting in her purse behind an old library card.
scenes.image_prompt: close on a woman's hands holding an open wallet, one plain bank card half pulled out from behind an older worn card

scenes.narration: It takes two seconds. There is no ceremony to it. The machine beeps, the man says thanks, and that is the whole thing.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket over a grey sweater, tapping a bank card on a reader held out by a mechanic across a repair shop counter, face carefully neutral, not looking at the machine

scenes.narration: Driving home she feels lucky. This is exactly what a credit card is for. This is the system working, and she has used it correctly.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, a plain dark green jacket over a grey sweater, driving a small faded red hatchback, calm, afternoon light through the windshield

scenes.narration: That night she does the math at her kitchen table, which is a thing she is good at and does not enjoy.
scenes.image_prompt: a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, a wooden table under the window, two mismatched chairs, and a corkboard covered in pinned paper, evening, one lamp on

scenes.narration: Six hundred dollars. She will clear it over three months. Two hundred a month is manageable if she is careful about groceries.
scenes.image_prompt: close on a woman's hands writing figures in a lined notebook on a wooden kitchen table, a calculator beside it

scenes.narration: She closes the notebook feeling organised. Nothing about this evening is a mistake. That is the part worth remembering later.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, a grey sweater, closing a notebook at a wooden table in a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, calm expression

scenes.narration: Month two. The minimum payment arrives.
scenes.image_prompt: the words MONTH TWO in large plain black capitals, centred, nothing else

scenes.narration: The statement says she owes six hundred and eleven dollars. It also says her minimum payment is thirty dollars and forty cents.
scenes.image_prompt: a printed bank statement lying on a wooden kitchen table under a window, a mug beside it, morning light

scenes.narration: Thirty dollars. Not two hundred. Thirty. She reads it twice to check she has understood, because it seems too small to be true.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, a grey sweater, holding a printed statement close, reading it, slight frown, small kitchen with pale yellow walls behind her

scenes.narration: She pays the thirty. It would be strange not to. The bill said thirty and she paid thirty, and everything about that is correct.
scenes.image_prompt: close on a woman's hands holding a phone showing a banking app payment screen, a printed statement on a wooden table beneath, small kitchen with pale yellow walls behind

scenes.narration: There is a small, real relief in it. She has an extra hundred and seventy dollars this month that she did not expect to have.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, a grey sweater, sitting back in a mismatched chair at a wooden kitchen table, shoulders down, quietly relieved

scenes.narration: Month five. The balance has not moved.
scenes.image_prompt: the words MONTH FIVE in large plain black capitals, centred, nothing else

scenes.narration: A tooth breaks in March. The dentist is two hundred and eighty dollars, and there is no version of this where she does not go.
scenes.image_prompt: a small dental waiting room with a row of empty chairs, a low table of magazines, a frosted glass door, harsh ceiling light

scenes.narration: She uses the card. It is the same two seconds as before. It is easier the second time, and easier again after that.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket, tapping a bank card on a reader at a dental reception desk, expression flat and practised, receptionist half turned away

scenes.narration: Her nephew turns six in April. She is not going to be the aunt who does not turn up with something.
scenes.image_prompt: a kitchen table laid for a child's birthday, a small cake with six candles lit, paper plates, a bright paper banner across the wall behind

scenes.narration: At the party she checks the balance out of habit. Nine hundred and forty dollars. She has paid a hundred and fifty this year.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a grey sweater, standing slightly apart at a child's birthday party, looking down at her phone screen, face fallen, the lit party out of focus behind her

scenes.narration: Back at her own table she works out what is actually happening, and it takes her about four minutes, because she is good at this.
scenes.image_prompt: a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, a wooden table under the window, papers and a calculator spread across it, evening, one lamp on

scenes.narration: The minimum payment is one percent of the balance, plus the interest. So as the balance falls, the payment falls with it.
scenes.image_prompt: close on a woman's hand resting on a sheet of paper covered in handwritten sums on a wooden kitchen table, pen down, still, pale yellow wall behind

scenes.narration: Which means it never ends. Paying the minimum is not slow progress. It is a treadmill set to exactly the speed you walk.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, a grey sweater, sitting back from a paper covered kitchen table, staring at nothing, one lamp on

scenes.narration: Month seven. She applies for a second card.
scenes.image_prompt: the words MONTH SEVEN in large plain black capitals, centred, nothing else

scenes.narration: There is an offer in her email. Zero percent on balance transfers for eighteen months. She reads it three times.
scenes.image_prompt: a dim living room at night, a woman sitting alone on a sofa, the only light coming from the phone in her hands

scenes.narration: It is not a trick. It is a real offer and the terms are exactly what they say. She is not being fooled by anything.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, her face lit from below by a phone screen in a dim living room at night, reading intently, eyes moving

scenes.narration: The application takes eleven minutes. She is approved before she has finished the washing up, which she takes as a good sign.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a grey sweater, standing at a kitchen sink in a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, one hand in soapy water, the other holding a phone, eyebrows up, faintly hopeful

scenes.narration: She moves the debt across. The first card reads zero. She looks at that zero for longer than she needs to.
scenes.image_prompt: close on a phone screen held in a woman's hands showing a single large balance of zero, kitchen out of focus behind

scenes.narration: This is the second time she feels rescued. It is the same feeling as the garage. It is also the last time she will feel it.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, a grey sweater, standing in a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, phone lowered, eyes closed, relieved

scenes.narration: Month eleven. The old card is not empty any more.
scenes.image_prompt: the words MONTH ELEVEN in large plain black capitals, centred, nothing else

scenes.narration: The first card did not stay at zero. Nobody closed it. It sat in her purse with a two thousand dollar limit and nothing on it.
scenes.image_prompt: a wide supermarket aisle, shelves on both sides, strip lighting, a single trolley halfway down, nobody else in the aisle

scenes.narration: A card with nothing on it does not feel like debt. It feels like a cushion. And cushions are for leaning on.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket, standing at a supermarket checkout with a half full trolley, looking down at a bank card in her hand, expression untroubled, almost absent

scenes.narration: She pays for the groceries in four instalments. Thirty one dollars now instead of a hundred and twenty four, which is plainly better.
scenes.image_prompt: close on a phone screen held in a woman's hands at a supermarket checkout showing a payment split into four smaller amounts, conveyor belt and shopping below

scenes.narration: She is not being reckless. She is solving this week using next week, over and over, and every single time it works.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket, walking out of a supermarket into grey daylight carrying two paper grocery bags, face composed, walking quickly

scenes.narration: She stops checking the balance around here. Not denial exactly. More that knowing the number does not change the number.
scenes.image_prompt: a dark bedroom at night, a single bed, curtains not quite closed, a thin line of streetlight across the wall

scenes.narration: She sleeps badly and blames work. It is not work. It is a figure she has decided not to look at.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears lying awake in bed in a dark bedroom, eyes open, staring up at the ceiling, a thin line of streetlight across the wall

scenes.narration: The phone lies face down on the bedside table. That is a small thing, and she does not notice she has started doing it.
scenes.image_prompt: close on a phone lying face down on a cluttered bedside table in a dark bedroom, a glass of water beside it, thin streetlight across the wall

scenes.narration: Month fourteen. There is a letter on the mat.
scenes.image_prompt: the words MONTH FOURTEEN in large plain black capitals, centred, nothing else

scenes.narration: She knows what it is from the envelope. Everyone knows what those envelopes are. She steps over it and goes to work.
scenes.image_prompt: a narrow hallway seen from above just inside a front door, one white envelope lying alone on the doormat, coats on hooks along the wall

scenes.narration: It sits on the table for four days. On the fifth she opens it standing up, because sitting down would make it a bigger thing.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a grey sweater, standing at a wooden table in a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, tearing open a white envelope, not sitting, mouth pressed thin

scenes.narration: The zero percent has ended. It ended a month ago. She has been paying nearly twenty five percent for five weeks without noticing.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, reading a letter held in both hands, face still, small kitchen with pale yellow walls behind her

scenes.narration: She sits down after all. The total across both cards is three thousand one hundred dollars. The car repair was six hundred.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a grey sweater, sitting down slowly into a mismatched chair at a wooden table in a small kitchen with pale yellow walls, letter loose in one hand, staring at nothing

scenes.narration: Month eighteen. The car is gone.
scenes.image_prompt: the words MONTH EIGHTEEN in large plain black capitals, centred, nothing else

scenes.narration: She sold the car in the end. Not for the money exactly. For the insurance and the gas and the registration, which were the parts she could still control.
scenes.image_prompt: an empty parking space on a residential street in the rain, a dark oil stain on the tarmac where a car used to sit

scenes.narration: The repair she borrowed six hundred dollars for lasted eleven months. Then she sold the car to keep up the payments on the borrowing.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair tucked behind her ears, a plain dark green jacket over a grey sweater, standing alone at a bus stop shelter in the rain, looking down the empty road, face tired and unbothered

scenes.narration: She is not ruined. That is worth saying plainly. She goes to work and pays her rent and nothing dramatic has happened to her at all.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair, a plain dark green jacket, sitting on a bus by the window, ordinary expression, grey light outside

scenes.narration: But if she only ever pays the minimum, that three thousand one hundred takes almost sixteen years to clear, and she will pay back eight thousand four hundred dollars.
scenes.image_prompt: a woman in her early thirties with short dark hair seen from behind, sitting on a bus, looking out of a rain streaked window at passing houses

scenes.narration: None of it was a mistake. That is the thing about this. There was never a single day where the wrong choice was the obvious one.
scenes.image_prompt: a bus pulling away down a wet grey street seen from a distance, tail lights on, ordinary houses on both sides
